_comment: Conformance cases for the gateway role: one held bundle, one call, and what the caller and Rail Center get. Taken from datrail/gateway's gateway-core/tests/core_support.py, ENFORCEMENT_CASES, at d6ae488 (master), dumped losslessly: `bundle` is the object the case hands to validate_bundle, null where none is held; `key_set` the JWKS signed tickets are checked against, null where the gateway holds none; `request` the call as the Apigee servicer's table test sends it, `x_rail` and `x_rail_status` each header's values as sent and `headers` every other header as (name, value) pairs. `expect.status` is the refusal's, null where the call is forwarded, with its body in `refusal_body`; `expect.report` is the denial report less `denied_at`, null where none is sent; `expect.python_logged` holds parts of one line the Python gateway logs, for reference: this gateway's log text differs. `not_for` names the Python interfaces a case is skipped for, and why. Tickets are judged at any time from 1700000000 (their `nbf`) to before 4102444800 (their `exp`). Removed: 3 with a 1.x bundle (`v1, no ticket, the chain's rule decides`, `v1, a flat claim`, `v1, a v2 condition is uninterpretable`), since only 2.0 and later is read. Checked when dumped: the Python Apigee servicer passes all 89 cases from this file alone. This file is now the source.
